author: Chapin Jewell News & Tribune Correspondent
title: Philip Barbour girls defeat Frankfort, 7-1, to open playoffs | Mineral County WV News and Tribune | wvnews.com
text:
SHORT GAP, W.Va. (WV News) – The Philip Barbour Lady Colts won their first game of the season, against Tyler Consolidated, on Aug. 20. They waited 63 days to get another one, but it would come at the most important of times, a 7-1, first-round regional game at Frankfort.
With the win, Philip Barbour advances to play top-seeded Lincoln on Saturday, Oct. 25.
Philip Barbour, the No. 5 seed, entered the contest after posting a regular season record of 1-17-1, and again, that one win came in the first game of the season over Tyler Consolidated.
Frankfort, the No. 4 seed, entered the contest after posting a regular season record of 3-15-1 with one win each at the bear the beginning, in the middle, and near the end of the season.
“We played a Big 10 schedule mostly, not getting many regional games, so we were playing up so much this season against those bigger AAA schools. We’ve taken our licks, but I kept reassuring the girls, we’re going to get there,” Philip Barbour coach Phil Perkins stated.
According to Perkins, “We’ve got a young team, but they’ve come a long way this season. We took our licks, but just kept trying to fight through and build and develop the girls and the program. These girls play with their heart, and it showed tonight.”
“The girls are on cloud nine, but we’re trying to stay focused and stay humble. But. We’re ecstatic about our win tonight,” Perkins noted.
It took 22 minutes and two seconds for Philip Barbour to break the seal on a scoreless tie, but their first goal came at the 17:58 mark of the first half when Aubrey Andrews scored to give the Lady Colts the 1-0 lead. 13 minutes and 10 seconds later (4:48), Philip Barbour scored again when Madalynn Wolfe seized the opportunity and delivered a strike to put the Lady Colts up 2-0.
Frankfort wasted little time, 24 seconds to be exact (4:24), when Karina Metz scored a goal off an assist by Regan Getz. With the score, the Falcons cut Philip Barbour’s lead to 2-1.
Exactly one minute later (3:24), Gracie Howell scored for Philip Barbour off an assist from Aubrey Andrews to extend the Lady Colts’ lead back out to two goals, 3-1. Philip Barbour had one more in the chamber before halftime, and with 26.9 seconds before the break, Madalynn Wolfe, off an assist by Aubrey Andrews, gave the Lady Colts a 4-1 lead at the half.
After the break, Philip Barbour went straight to work, when, just 50 seconds in (39:10), Emma Carter scored a rainbow goal to extend the Lady Colts’ lead to 5-1. Carter would score another rainbow goal sometime later, giving Philip Barbour the 6-1 lead. With 7:30, Carter again scored from the left side of the box, pushing the lead out to six goals, 7-1, for good.
With the loss, Frankfort’s season concludes with an overall record of 3-16-1. There were highlights, and qualifying to host a playoff game was one of them.
“The difference between the first game and the last few games is night and day. They’ve come
a long way. A lot of these girls don’t have a lot of experience, and they’ve given it all they’ve had. They never quit on a single game, and a lot of them are coming back next year,” Frankfort coach Chris Brooks stated.
According to Brooks, “The girls we’re losing, like Meghann Griffith and Niya Lantz, they will be some pretty big losses. Kailynn Crone and Aubrey Haddix, they came out and played for us for three years, they weren’t soccer players to begin with, but playing this game tonight, you couldn’t tell that. They gave it all they had.”
